In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a concurrency control scheme that can handle the high-speed environment, and that can perform very well in a mixed workload environment, which includes a significant number of update transactions.
the development of a CC protocol that performs well in a high-speed environment.
the design and analysis of CC protocols for DDBS operating on high-speed wide area computer networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
datacycling is a very efficient CC protocol in high-speed wide-area networks, especially for read-oriented transactions.
datacycle is an excellent choice for a read-intensive environment and a hybrid protocol is a good choice for a mixed read and write workload.
the send-on-demand protocol is a very promising concurrency control protocol, and is a good alternative to locking for DDBS applications in high-speed wide-area networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
datacycling can perform well in a read oriented environment, but the performance is very sensitive to the ratio of read/write transactions.
the datacycle scheme performs better than locking, and that a hybrid scheme performs best in a read-dominated environment.
the send-on-demand protocol is the best choice in a high-speed network environment, where communication latency is the dominant factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a datacycle scheme is a good candidate for a CC protocol for high-speed wide area networked DDBS.
the datacycle scheme performs better than other schemes for queries, but for update intensive applications the performance of all schemes is comparable.
datacycling is a viable concurrency control mechanism for high-speed distributed database systems.
